connectors.name: Gmail
connectors.notes: Create your own Google Cloud OAuth client (type Web application, with 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' ticked) and enable gmail.googleapis.com + gmailmcp.googleapis.com. Drafts only: the server cannot send.

guide.summary: Google's official Gmail MCP server. Each Google account (personal Gmail or Workspace) becomes one hydra-mcp account.
before: A Google Cloud project (free). One project and one OAuth client serve every Google connector and every Google account.
About 10 minutes the first time, to create that OAuth client. The next Gmail or Google accounts connect in one click.
If Google answers that the API is not available for your account, enroll it in the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program (link below): Google has run the Workspace MCP servers as a preview.
guide.accounts: Add as many Google accounts as you like. In Testing mode, each address must first be added as a test user on the consent screen.
gotchas: Client type: Web application. Google rejects calls from an OAuth client unless 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' is ticked on it (Google Auth Platform, Clients). The default Apps Script client cannot have this setting.
APIs to enable: gmail.googleapis.com and gmailmcp.googleapis.com.
Scopes asked: gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.modify (the server advertises about 20, including full mailbox access; hydra-mcp asks only for these three).
Tools: search and read threads and messages, drafts, labels, trash, spam. No send tool: the AI writes a draft, you send it from Gmail.
hydra-mcp asks Google for offline access, so it gets a refresh token and you do not log in again every hour.

Testing-mode apps: Google may expire refresh tokens after 7 days. If an account turns 'not connected', click Reconnect, or publish the consent screen to 'In production' (no review needed for personal use under 100 users, but Google shows an 'unverified app' warning).
Google recommends screening tool results for prompt injection (Model Armor or similar): mail content is untrusted input for the AI.

connectors.name: Atlassian (Jira, Confluence)
connectors.notes: Tokens are bound to one site (cloudId): one account per Atlassian site.

guide.summary: Atlassian's official Rovo MCP server: Jira, Confluence, Compass, plus Teamwork Graph search. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you log in at Atlassian.
before: An Atlassian Cloud site (xxx.atlassian.net). Server and Data Center are not supported.
Your site admin may restrict which apps can connect. If the consent page says access is denied, ask them to allow the Atlassian Rovo MCP server for your site.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Atlassian site: the login is granted on the site you pick on the consent page. To add another site, click '+ Add another account' and choose the other site there. hydra-mcp reads the site name to label the account.
gotchas: On the consent page, check which site is selected in the dropdown before you click Accept: it decides which site this account reaches.
Some tools (enriched Teamwork Graph calls) consume Rovo credits of your site.
Atlassian moves remaining v1 clients to the v2 tools on 1 March 2027. hydra-mcp already uses v2.
API tokens (email + token, Basic auth) also exist, but only if your org admin enables them. OAuth is Atlassian's recommended way and is what hydra-mcp uses.

links.label: Get started with the Atlassian Rovo MCP server
Admin: control the MCP server settings

connectors.name: Linear
connectors.notes: One account per workspace. Read-only variant: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly. Also accepts a Linear API key as bearer.

guide.summary: Linear's official MCP server: issues, projects, cycles, comments. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you log in at Linear.
before: A Linear account. No plan or admin approval is needed for the standard login.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Linear workspace. To add another workspace, click '+ Add another account' and pick the other workspace on Linear's consent page.
gotchas: Linear's OAuth sessions start with a 25-day refresh window. If an account turns 'not connected', click Reconnect.

Read-only: add https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly by URL (it only ever exposes read tools), or use a Linear API key with only the Read permission ('Use a token instead'). A read-only grant in hydra-mcp also hides write tools.
Linear's own docs mention mcp-remote config folders for several workspaces: not needed here, each hydra-mcp account keeps its own token.

token.name: Linear API key
token.how: Linear, Settings, Security & access, Personal API keys, New key. Pick the workspace and the permissions (Read only is enough to search). Copy the key (lin_api_...).

connectors.name: Notion
connectors.notes: Supports DCR and Client ID Metadata Documents. The legacy SSE endpoint (/sse) retires on 23 February 2027; hydra-mcp uses /mcp.

guide.summary: Notion's official hosted MCP server: search, read and edit pages and databases. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you log in at Notion.
before: You must be a member of the workspace. Guests cannot connect.
The AI sees exactly what your Notion user can see in the workspace you pick.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Notion workspace: pick the workspace on Notion's consent page.
gotchas: Search across connected sources (Slack, Google Drive...) and some search filters need a Business or Enterprise plan with Notion AI.
Business and Enterprise plans get higher rate limits.
File uploads through the tools are limited to 20 MiB.
MCP tokens (no browser login) exist on Business and Enterprise only, and only workspace owners can create them.
An Enterprise workspace policy can block MCP connections: ask your workspace owner if the consent page refuses.
The older open-source notion-mcp-server (integration token) is no longer maintained: use this hosted one.

token.name: Notion MCP token (Business and Enterprise)
token.how: A workspace owner creates it in Notion's Developer portal with 'New MCP token'. Paste it here; no browser login is needed.

connectors.name: GitHub
connectors.notes: No dynamic registration: create a GitHub OAuth App once, or connect with a personal access token. Keep the trailing slash.

guide.summary: GitHub's official remote MCP server: repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, code search. GitHub does not let apps register themselves, so choose one of two ways.
before: Fastest: a personal access token (2 minutes, nothing to register). Click 'Use a token instead'.
Or a GitHub OAuth App (5 minutes, once): then every GitHub account signs in with one click, like in Claude.
Organization repositories: the org may require owner approval for OAuth Apps, or for fine-grained tokens. Check Organization settings, Third-party access.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per GitHub user (or per token). hydra-mcp labels it with the GitHub login.
gotchas: The OAuth consent screen lists broad classic scopes (repo, read:org, gist, notifications...). For narrow access, use a fine-grained token restricted to some repositories.
Fine-grained tokens expire (you choose the date, up to a year). When one expires, the account shows 'not connected': create a new token and click 'New token' on that account.

Fewer tools: GitHub serves one URL per toolset, for example https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/x/issues or /mcp/x/pull_requests, and /readonly after any of them (/mcp/readonly, /mcp/x/issues/readonly). Add such a URL as 'Another MCP server (by URL)'. Your AI then gets fewer, more relevant tools.
GitHub Enterprise Server is not supported by the remote server. GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency uses another host (copilot-api.<your-subdomain>.ghe.com/mcp): add it by URL, with a token.

token.name: GitHub personal access token
token.how: Fine-grained token: name it hydra-mcp, pick an expiration, choose the resource owner and the repositories, then under Repository permissions give Contents, Issues and Pull requests: Read (or Read and write). Metadata: Read is added automatically. Generate, then copy the token (github_pat_...). A classic token (ghp_..., scope repo) also works.

steps.title: Open 'Register a new OAuth app' on GitHub
steps.text: For an app owned by an organization instead of you: Organization settings, Developer settings, OAuth Apps, New OAuth App.

steps.title: Fill in the form
steps.text: Redirect URI is the callback below, not the homepage. Leave 'Allow wildcard matching' and 'Enable Device Flow' unticked. Tick 'Expire user access tokens': GitHub then issues 8-hour tokens with a refresh token, which hydra-mcp renews on its own (unticked works too: tokens never expire). Then click Register application.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.text: On the app's page, copy the Client ID, then click 'Generate a new client secret' and copy it now: GitHub shows it only once.

steps.title: Paste the client ID and secret below
steps.text: The secret is stored encrypted on this machine. Then GitHub asks you to authorize hydra-mcp. For organization repositories, use 'Request' or 'Grant' next to the org on that page.

connectors.name: Slack
connectors.notes: No dynamic registration. You create a Slack app in your workspace (internal apps are allowed for MCP, unlisted distributed apps are not), turn on its MCP feature, and a workspace admin approves it. One app per workspace.

guide.summary: Slack's official MCP server: search messages and files, read channels and threads, send and schedule messages, canvases, lists, reactions. It acts as you (user token): the AI sees what you see.
before: A workspace admin must allow MCP integrations, and approve your app if your workspace requires app approval. On a workspace you own, you approve it yourself.
About 5 minutes per workspace, to create a small Slack app. Slack does not let apps register themselves, and only lets an app you created be used in its own workspace.
IP allowlists of your workspace apply to MCP calls too: the machine running hydra-mcp must be allowed.
guide.accounts: One Slack app per workspace. For a second workspace, click '+ Another workspace' on the Slack card: hydra-mcp adds a second Slack server with its own app, and its tools appear as slack-2__… . A second person in the same workspace is '+ Add another account' (same app).
gotchas: Turn on PKCE in the app (OAuth & Permissions): Slack only accepts a plain-http callback on localhost from apps with PKCE, which is why the callback below says localhost and not 127.0.0.1. PKCE makes the app a public client, cannot be undone, and its refresh tokens last 30 days. Leave the client secret empty in hydra-mcp then.
Behind an HTTPS public URL (a tunnel, see the Claude guides) you can skip PKCE: register that https callback and paste the client secret instead.

Scopes: hydra-mcp asks for every user scope the Slack tools document (search, history, write...). Remove the ones you do not want from the app's User Token Scopes before installing; tools that need them will then fail. Read-only use: also give your AI app a 'read only' grant in hydra-mcp.
The consent page shows the workspace in its top right corner: check it before you click Allow. hydra-mcp labels the account with the workspace name.
Slack rejects apps that are distributed but not published in the Slack Marketplace: keep 'Manage Distribution' off.

steps.title: Create the Slack app from a manifest
steps.text: Click 'Create New App', choose 'From a manifest', pick the workspace this account is in, select the JSON tab and replace its content with the manifest below. It sets the name, the callback and the user scopes. Review, then Create.

steps.title: Turn on MCP for the app
steps.text: In the app's sidebar, open 'Agents' and switch on 'Slack Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server'.

steps.title: Opt in to PKCE
steps.text: OAuth & Permissions: opt in to PKCE. Slack accepts the plain-http localhost callback only from PKCE apps. This makes the app a public client and cannot be undone, which is fine for an app used only by hydra-mcp. Skip this step if hydra-mcp runs behind an https public URL.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID
steps.text: Basic Information, App Credentials: copy the Client ID. With PKCE on, leave the secret empty below. Without PKCE, also copy the Client Secret.

steps.title: Paste it below, then allow access
steps.text: Slack shows its consent page for your workspace. If it says the app needs approval, your admin approves it in the workspace's app management; then click Reconnect.

links.label: Developing with the Slack MCP server
Guide to MCP in Slack (Help Center)

guide.summary: Sentry's official MCP server: issues, events, traces, releases, and Seer analysis. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you log in at Sentry.
before: A sentry.io account. Self-hosted Sentry is not served by this remote server (Sentry's CLI offers a local one).
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Sentry login. To keep two organizations apart, add each by URL scoped to it: https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp/<org-slug> (or /<org-slug>/<project-slug>, which Sentry recommends).
gotchas: Sentry offers no token login for the remote server: OAuth only.
Add ?experimental=1 to the URL to get Sentry's experimental tools.

connectors.name: Stripe
connectors.notes: OAuth refresh tokens expire after 14 days. Restricted agent API key also accepted as bearer.

guide.summary: Stripe's official MCP server: customers, payments, invoices, subscriptions, docs search. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you approve access in Stripe.
before: A Stripe account. Team admins can switch MCP access off, separately for live mode and sandboxes: Dashboard, Settings, MCP and CLI access.
Start with a sandbox: on the consent page you choose live or sandbox and the permissions per environment.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Stripe account and environment you approve.
gotchas: Stripe's OAuth sessions last 14 days at most, refresh included: after that the account shows 'not connected' and you click Reconnect. An agent API key avoids this.
Sensitive actions such as refunds ask for a confirmation in the Stripe Dashboard, through a link the AI gives you. It expires after 24 hours.
From 11 January 2027, Stripe MCP only accepts OAuth or agent API keys: full secret keys (sk_...) and plain restricted keys stop working.
Connect platforms: OAuth cannot act on connected accounts; use an agent API key.

token.name: Stripe agent API key
token.how: In the Stripe Dashboard, create an agent API key with only the permissions you want the AI to have (it shows an 'Agent' badge). Paste it here.

connectors.name: Asana
connectors.notes: No dynamic client registration on v2: create an MCP app in the Asana developer console.

guide.summary: Asana's official MCP server (v2): tasks, projects, goals, portfolios. Asana does not let apps register themselves: you create an Asana app once.
before: About 5 minutes once, in Asana's developer console, to create the app hydra-mcp signs in with.
Your workspace admin may block MCP clients in App management (Enterprise). If the login says the app is blocked, ask them to allow it.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Asana login; it reaches the workspaces that user belongs to.
gotchas: 'Client not found' at login: the client ID is wrong or the app was deleted. Use 'Reset' on the server (Advanced) and paste a new one.
The old v1 endpoint (mcp.asana.com/sse) is shut down; hydra-mcp uses v2.
Asana has no token login for the v2 MCP server.

steps.title: Read Asana's MCP integration guide
steps.text: It shows which app type to pick for an MCP client. Keep it open next to the console.

steps.title: Create the app in the developer console
steps.text: My apps, Create new app, name it hydra-mcp. In its OAuth settings, add this redirect URL.

steps.title: Paste the client ID and secret below
steps.text: Both are on the app's OAuth page. The secret is stored encrypted on this machine.

connectors.name: Cloudflare API
connectors.notes: Also accepts a Cloudflare API token as bearer. Product-specific servers exist (docs, browser, containers...).

guide.summary: Cloudflare's API MCP server: the whole Cloudflare API (2,500+ endpoints) through search and execute tools. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you pick the permissions at Cloudflare.
before: A Cloudflare account. On the consent page you choose which permissions the AI gets: grant the least you need.
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Cloudflare login, or per API token.
gotchas: The execute tool runs JavaScript the AI writes against the Cloudflare API, in an isolated sandbox. With write permissions it can change DNS, Workers, etc. Give a read-only grant to clients that only need to look.
Product servers (docs, browser, containers...) have their own URLs, e.g. https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp: add them by URL.

token.name: Cloudflare API token
token.how: My Profile, API Tokens, Create Token. Start from a template or pick permissions and accounts. User tokens and account tokens both work.

connectors.name: Supabase
connectors.notes: Optional query params: project_ref, read_only=true, features.

guide.summary: Supabase's official MCP server: projects, SQL, migrations, Edge Functions, logs, docs. One click: hydra-mcp registers itself, you pick the organization at Supabase.
before: A Supabase account. On the consent page, choose the organization that holds your project.
Supabase strongly advises against connecting production data. Use a dev project, or scope and lock it down (see below).
guide.accounts: One hydra-mcp account per Supabase organization you approve, or per access token.
gotchas: Safer URL: add it by URL with ?project_ref=<id>&read_only=true to reach one project, read-only. features=<groups> limits the tool groups.
Branching tools need a paid plan. Storage tools are off by default.
Confirmation forms before risky tools are a guardrail, not a guarantee.

token.name: Supabase personal access token
token.how: Account, Access Tokens, Generate new token. Supabase recommends also scoping the server URL with ?project_ref=<id>.
